subject: Legal + Procurement sequencing: MSA / DPA / Order Form tight-coupling and checkpoints
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Legal + Procurement sequencing: MSA / DPA / Order Form tight-coupling and checkpoints

Hi Samantha / Jason —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our call we want to make the sequencing explicit so procurement, legal, and the product team have a predictable path to signature and activation. Attached are: (1) a working MAP (MAP-Novamed-v3.xlsx) showing gated milestones, (2) our redline summary (redwood_MSA_comments_v2.pdf), and (3) a draft order form.

Key asks from our side so we can lock the timeline:
- Can Novamed confirm whether procurement requires countersignature on the Order Form before the DPA is fully accepted?
- Is there a single procurement PO path or do you need a multi-stage PO tied to the pilot?
- Primary legal reviewers and expected SLA for review cycles (we usually plan 48–72h for each pass).

Proposed sequencing (high level):
1) Legal show-stopper review of MSA/DPA (T+3 business days window for initial comments)
2) Mutual action plan sign-off on milestones + order form terms (concurrent with final DPA pass)
3) Order form signature (DocuSign link will be sent once we have final SOW and order quantities)
4) Activation & pilot kickoff (target: two business days after signed order form)

I’ve cc’d Laura (legal) and Karthik (sales) to keep the loop tight. If we agree to the sequencing above I’ll publish a short MAP with owners and dates.

Thanks — Michael

Attachments: MAP-Novamed-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_MSA_comments_v2.pdf (pdf), order-form-draft.docx (docx)
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novamed.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Park <jason.park@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Legal + Procurement sequencing: MSA / DPA / Order Form tight-coupling and checkpoints

Michael —

Thanks for sending. Quick answers from procurement/legal here:
- Procurement prefers to receive an executed MSA + DPA prior to issuing a PO for anything beyond a pilot. For pilot purchases we can do a limited PO tied to pilot scope, but enterprise PO requires fully executed legal.
- We typically run legal reviews in parallel with procurement but procurement will not commit the full PO without the DPA signed (Novamed compliance policy).
- Primary reviewers: Jason Park (procurement lead) and myself; legal counsel (outside counsel) will review MSAs for any material changes. Expect ~3 business days for the first pass; faster if changes are limited to appendices.

Two asks from Novamed:
1) Would Redwood accept a pilot order form signed with an explicit bridge clause that allows a pilot and defers full commercial terms until MSA/DPA are signed?
2) Can Redwood provide a short matrix of which contract terms are "must-have" vs "negotiable" (we want to avoid full redlines on routine items).

If we can get that, I think we can align timelines. Targeting a pilot kickoff week of 21 June if paperwork is in place.

— Samantha
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Legal + Procurement sequencing: MSA / DPA / Order Form tight-coupling and checkpoints

Michael / Karthik —

Read Samantha’s note. High-level legal response and constraints (summary of redwood_MSA_comments_v2.pdf):
- Non-starters / must-have (we should press here): data residency clause alignment with their DPA schedule, limited liability cap (standard), and clear delineation of customer vs. provider responsibilities for data deletion.
- Negotiable items: indemnity reciprocity language (we can be flexible on scope tied to third-party claims), payment terms (we can accept their standard net-30 on pilot orders), and certain audit frequencies.

On the pilot-order bridge clause — we can support a narrowly-scoped pilot order form that limits liability exposure and includes an explicit carriage clause: pilot terms terminate automatically upon full commercial execution and do not create precedent for production pricing. I’ll draft a short pilot annex that meets that requirement.

I recommend the following checkpoints and owners in the MAP:
- Legal first-pass (Redwood, Laura) — due by 2025-06-05 EOD
- Novamed first-pass (Samantha/Jason) — target 2025-06-09
- Mutual sign-off on MAP (Michael/Samantha) — 2025-06-10
- Order form ready for signature (Redwood ops/Karthik) — 2025-06-12
- DocuSign circulation & execution (both parties) — target 2025-06-15

I’ll attach the short pilot annex and a terms matrix to my next note.

Laura

Attachment: redwood_MSA_comments_v2.pdf (highlighted)

Samantha / Jason —

Appreciate the clarity. Based on Laura’s draft and your preferences, attached is a concise MAP (spreadsheet link below) with owners and the pilot annex. Key changes from the previous attachment:

- Terms matrix (must-have vs negotiable) added as tab 2
- Proposed DocuSign envelope pre-populated for the order form and pilot annex — link below will be active once both parties confirm.

Proposed next steps (what I’ll do unless I hear otherwise by EOD tomorrow):

2) Laura to send the short pilot annex + terms matrix to Novamed legal (done).
3) Karthik to prepare order form with pilot quantities and pricing (target 2025-06-12).
4) Once Novamed confirms first-pass comments (target 2025-06-09) we will lock DocuSign for circulation (target 2025-06-15).

Links / attachments:

If that sequencing works, I’ll move the MAP into "action" and create calendar invites for the decision checkpoints.

Thanks — Michael
